text:
incident-bot: S1 PAGE — serving brownout + rapid autoscale churn in eu-west. Incident INC-2026-3457. Affected: hosted/text-generation models on gpu-pool-eu. Paging @christina_sre (primary), @michael_infra (infra), @raj_ml (runtime). :fire:

christina_sre: ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs and joining bridge.

raj_ml: seeing repeated CUDA OOM entries on several pods, then CrashLoopBackOff. GPU drivers look ok but memory usage spikes right before OOM.

michael_infra: autoscaler is thrashing — HPA + custom autoscaler bouncing replicas: 12 -> 38 -> 7 within ~2m. nodes flapped (kubelet eviction, then rejoin). Looks like scale-up overshoot then immediate scale-down when requests dip.

ada_sre: @christina_sre I'm going to temporarily disable cluster-autoscaler scale-to-zero and raise min-replicas while we stabilize.

christina_sre: do it. also set stabilization window for the custom autoscaler to 180s. we suspect too-short cooldowns triggering oscillation when some pods crash and are recreated.

deploy-bot: @christina_sre executed: kubectl patch hpa runtime-workers -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}' in eu-west

michael_infra: patch applied. also bumping minReplicas to 10 for runtime-workers deployment.

raj_ml: log snippet from runtime-worker-7 (gpu node gpu-eu-12):
```
[2026-03-15T09:14:23Z] runtime ERROR: Alloc failed: CudaError: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:14:23Z] kernel: oom-killer invoked for process runtime-worker
[2026-03-15T09:14:24Z] container runtime-worker-7 exited code 137
```

jen_support: Support ticket SUP-78912 opened — customer "FinCap" reporting 502s and high tail latency. Ops impact: some clients seeing large token-latency spikes, retries cause bursts. I've notified account exec @alex_sales.

alex_sales: thanks. keep me posted; I need to message FinCap with ETA and mitigation.

christina_sre: immediate mitigations:
- set minReplicas=10 (done)
- increase stabilizationWindowSeconds=180 (done)
- cordon node gpu-eu-12 (evict pods to avoid repeated OOM)
- change runtime deployment to use fallback model variant (cpu-quantized) for non-critical routes

michael_infra: cordoned node and draining now: kubectl cordon gpu-eu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force

raj_ml: switching routes for lower-tier traffic to rwd-medium-8q (quantized) to reduce memory while we stabilize. patching routing config now.

deploy-bot: routing config updated: prod-route:trafficSplit -> primary: rwd-large (70%), fallback: rwd-medium-8q (30%)

ada_sre: observed autoscaler logs: several scale-downs initiated by short window metric dips (request concurrency drops during crash/retry spikes). We'll also add a rate-limit guard to prevent scaling down more than 30% in 2m.

christina_sre: rolling restart of runtime-workers to flush bad state and restart kv caches. deploy-bot: please do a rolling restart with maxUnavailable=1.

deploy-bot: initiated: kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-workers --namespace=production (maxUnavailable=1)

raj_ml: after restart, memory burst pattern reduced for the restarted pods. new pods report stable GPU memory usage ~70% vs 98% before.

michael_infra: still seeing one pod crashloop on gpu-eu-14 with repeated OOM. isolating and setting pod priority lower so it doesn't evict others.

christina_sre: any sign of driver/kernel level failures?

raj_ml: kernel logs look clean aside from OOMs; driver versions consistent. suspect workload spike + autoscale oscillation leading to eviction cycles and insufficient warm-up of KV caches (cold model caches cause high allocation).

jen_support: FinCap reports partial recovery, latency dropping but intermittent 502s remain. I've opened a customer update: "We are mitigating and have temporarily shifted some traffic to quantized models; next update in 30m."

alex_sales: good. please add request for contact if they want a dedicated tranche of capacity — we should offer reserved shards if heavy during trading hours.

christina_sre: action items while we keep incident open:
- stabilize autoscaler behavior (michael + ada)
- add pre-warm step for replicas to warm KV cache before redirecting traffic (raj + eng-runtime)
- investigate root cause of memory spikes on a subset of model versions (raj)
- postmortem and customer impact summary (christina + jen)

michael_infra: creating a short-term change to autoscaler config: set maxScaleDownRate=30% per 2m, set stabilizationWindowSeconds=180, disable scale-to-zero for gpu-pool-eu. I'll push PR to infra-config repo and roll out after +1 approval.

ada_sre: monitoring: put up temporary alert for repeated CrashLoopBackOff >3 pods in 5m and autoscaler thrash >3 scale events in 5m.

deploy-bot: alert rules created in prometheus: incident:autoscaler_thrash_eu > 3, incident:pod_crashloop_count > 3

raj_ml: workaround for immediate customer impact: pin critical route to pre-warmed dedicated pods (reserved capacity shard) for next 2h. switching now.

christina_sre: observed traffic now stable, scale chatter reduced. LAT p99 for text generation dropped from 1.8s to 600ms for affected routes. FinCap still seeing a few errors but overall improved.

jen_support: updating SUP-78912 with timeline and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3457 status: mitigated — low probability of recurrence with temp config. Will keep open for postmortem.

christina_sre: closing page for hands-on — handing to postmortem owner. Next steps: schedule follow-up doc, include experiment to add warm-up latency SLO and autoscaler guard rails. I'll create the postmortem and assign owners.

christina_sre: postmortem owner: christina_sre. timeline doc will be in #postmortems/incidents and I'll link SUP-78912. expected ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.

alex_sales: sending customer note now. thanks team. :thumbsup:

jen_support: tagging support follow-up: ensure FinCap gets root-cause summary and SLA credit evaluation if they request.

michael_infra: follow-up infra PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-config/pull/384 (autoscaler damping + minReplicas change).

ada_sre: will follow up with a longer-term plan: autoscaler hysteresis, rate-limited scale actions, and pre-warm hooks for models that have heavy KV caches.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3457 — moved to monitoring state. last update 1955500265."
